title: Local Markov Order and Global Inference in Many-Body Dynamics
abstract: We consider how the presence of conserved charges affects memory in a classical stochastic process, the symmetric exclusion process, with an observer constantly measuring a single site. We find that the observer's measurement record becomes Markovian (i.e., loses memory) on a timescale that depends on their knowledge of the global charge, namely the total particle number. In particular, when the global charge is unknown a priori, the observer's time series Markovianizes on a timescale constrained by their ability to learn it from their measurement record. Augmenting the observer's record with bulk measurements drives a charge-learnability transition between charge-fuzzy and -sharp phases. We show that the memory timescale tracks the learnability timescale, diverging in the fuzzy phase and remaining finite in the sharp phase.
summary: The paper analyzes how local measurements affect memory in charge-conserving many-body systems like the SEP. It finds that when the global charge is unknown, the system's memory decays slowly, tracking the time required for the observer to learn this hidden conserved quantity. This establishes a fundamental link between information acquisition and dynamical relaxation timescales.
main_problem: The study investigates how conserved charges influence memory (Markovianity) in a classical stochastic process when only local measurements are available to an observer.
main_result: The system's memory timescale tracks the rate at which the global charge can be learned from local measurements; this leads to distinct 'charge-fuzzy' and 'charge-sharp' phases.
method: Information-theoretic diagnostics, specifically analyzing the decay of Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) in relation to the measurement record.
model_or_system: The Symmetric Exclusion Process (SEP), a classical model for charge-conserving dynamics on a 1D lattice with hardcore particles. The analysis compares scenarios where the total particle number (charge) is fixed versus when it is unknown/hidden from the observer.
key_observables: Conditional Mutual Information (CMI), Posterior Entropy $H(N|B)$, and the effective dynamical exponent ($z_{	ext{eff}}$).
important_parameters: Measurement probability per time step ($p$), system size ($L$), and the transition point $p^\#$ marking charge learnability.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on relating memory decay to information acquisition, assuming that learning the global conserved quantity dictates the long-time dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate CMI decay plots showing scaling collapses for both fixed and hidden charge sectors. They also map out a phase diagram based on measurement probability $p$, demonstrating the flow of the effective dynamical exponent $z_{	ext{eff}}$ across the transition point $p^\#$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by analyzing CMI decay for both known and hidden global charges. It establishes that memory loss is governed by charge learnability, showing a divergence in memory time when the charge is unknown but finite when it can be learned.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful information-theoretic lens to study non-equilibrium dynamics, directly linking the rate of information acquisition (learning) to the relaxation timescale (memory), which has analogues in quantum measurement theory and open quantum systems.
